deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. These are working notes from meridian-instrument observations. The instrument has a vertical circle read by a vernier (degrees, minutes, rough seconds) and two micrometer microscopes (fine seconds), plus a level ('Libelle'). Each star is timed over three wires of the transit, and a barometer and Réaumur thermometer reading is taken for refraction. Saturday the 25th following Friday 'April 24' (previous page) fits the years 1812, 1818 and 1829. The latitude obtained is about 51°32', which fits Göttingen.

The previous page notes that the circle was reversed and the collimation adjusted on a tree trunk. The 'Spitze des Baums' readings here continue that programme.

(A) Saturday 25: 'Die Mikroskope berichtigt' (the microscopes were adjusted), then a level determination of the zenith (vertical) point.
- The circle is read in two positions of the level: 'Spitze innen' (point inside) and 'Spitze aussen' (point outside).
- Each position gives three readings (vernier, microscope A, microscope B): innen 9'11.8", 3'34.7", 3'21.4"; aussen 9'8.0", 3'30.2", 3'18.0".
- Each position also has a bubble correction: innen −0.8", aussen +1.4".
- [My reconstruction, verified numerically:] the corrected readings are averaged. Vernier: (551.0 + 549.4)/2 = 550.2" = 9'10.2". Microscope A: (213.9 + 211.6)/2 = 212.75" = 3'32.75". Microscope B: (200.6 + 199.4)/2 = 200.0" = 3'20.0".
- So the circle reads 0°9'10.2" etc. when the line of sight is vertical. This is the index (zenith-point) error.

(B) Sunday 26. For each star the entries are three wire times (minutes and seconds, middle wire with hours), then || circle reading, two microscope readings, then barometer (Paris inches^z, lines^l) and thermometer (°R).
- Sirius: wires 36'55.2", 6h37'12.1", 37'29.1". The mean of the outer wires, 37'12.15", agrees with the middle wire; the wire intervals are 16.9 s and 17.0 s. Circle 68°7'42.3", microscopes 2'10.7", 1'48.8".
- New level determination: innen 9'10.0", 3'33.7", 3'16.9"; aussen correction −1.4". Mean = reading − 0.7" gives 9'9.3", 3'33.0", 3'16.2" (checked).
- Pollux: wires 33'56.9", 7h34'15.1", 34'33.8" (intervals 18.2 s and 18.7 s, about 17 s × sec δ). Circle 23°13'28.0", microscopes 2'53.4", 2'34.0".

Pollux latitude reduction:
- Apparent zenith distance = reading − zenith point. Vernier: 23°13'28.0" − 9'9.3" = 23°4'18.7".
- Fine seconds from the microscopes [my reconstruction]: (2'53.4" − 3'33.0") mod 60 = 20.4" and (2'34.0" − 3'16.2") mod 60 = 17.8". Their mean is 19.1".
- So z_app ≈ 23°4'19.1". Gauss's figure implies 19.04"; the 0.06" gap is probably a micrometer-scale correction.
- Add refraction (written 'Refr. 24.04"', for B = 27^z5.1^l, T = 11.2°R): z = 23°4'43.08".
- Add the adopted declination of Pollux, δ = 28°27'31.07": φ = z + δ = 51°32'14.15".
- The manuscript digits are overwritten ('1̶4', '4̶2'). Only the readings 23°4'43.08" and 51°32'14.15" are consistent with the circle reading minus 9'9". The result agrees with the next page's Polaris value 51°32'15.72".

Other stars:
- α Cygni 'i.P.' (lower culmination; the clock reads 8h35 against RA ≈ 20h35): wires 34'55.5", 35'18.5", 35'41" (intervals 23.0 s and 22.5 s, about 17 s × sec 44.6°). Circle about −83°35' (north side, rough). Three seconds readings follow.
- α Hydrae: wires 18'28.0", 9h18'44.1", 19'1.0"; circle 59°32'25". Then z ≈ 59°23'16" + about 1'36" refraction, giving δ ≈ −7°53', which matches α Hya around 1818.
- ο Leonis: no times; circle 40°57'39", microscopes 2'5.9", 1'46.4".
- Terrestrial mark ('Spitze des Baums im Meridian', the treetop in the meridian): 89°17'59" and 89°17'42", nearly horizontal. This mark is used to monitor collimation and azimuth.
- Regulus: wires 58'30.2", 9h58'46.4", 59'3.4"; circle 38°49'33", microscopes 3'57.8", 3'38.3". The vernier gives 38°40'23.7" and the microscopes give (24.8" + 22.1")/2 = 23.45", so they agree. With about 46" refraction and δ ≈ 12°50.5' this gives φ ≈ 51°31.7'.
- 'Gang der Uhr 1.66"': daily clock rate.
- β Cassiopeiae (written 'b Cassiop'), lower culmination at 11h59 against RA ≈ 0h: wires 59'3.1", 11h59'34.3", 60'5.1"; circle about 70°10'. The expected z is 180° − φ − δ ≈ 70°20', i.e. reading + index. Then come three seconds readings with signs, and the meteorology.

PURPOSE: to fix the zenith point of the circle and then derive latitude (and clock/azimuth checks) from stars of known declination at upper and lower culmination. This is continued on the next page with Polaris.
errors: No genuine computational errors found; all level means and the Pollux addition check exactly.

Pollux zenith distance and the latitude sum carry overwritten digits. As written in the transcription (23°14'43.08", 51°42'14.15") they are internally consistent but 10' too large. The context (index 9'9.3", next page's Polaris latitude 51°32'15.72") shows the intended values are 23°4'43.08" and 51°32'14.15".
My microscope-based reduction of Pollux gives 23°4'19.1" + 24.04" = 23°4'43.14", against Gauss's 43.08". The 0.06" gap is unexplained, perhaps a micrometer screw-value or run correction not shown.
For Sirius the microscope mean (35.15") and vernier seconds (33.0") differ by about 2". This is ordinary reading scatter, not a slip.

The latitude (about 51°32'14"–15") is roughly 27" larger than Gauss's definitive Göttingen value 51°31'47.85". It reflects a provisional index or instrumental error at this stage, not an arithmetic mistake.

results.what: Zenith point (index error) of a vertical circle from readings in two level positions, averaging bubble-corrected readings of vernier and two microscopes
results.modern_name: Index/level correction of a meridian circle (zenith-point determination)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th–19th c. practical astronomy (Reichenbach/Repsold instrument practice)

results.what: Latitude from meridian zenith distance of a star of known declination: phi = z_app + refraction + delta (Pollux gives 51°32'14.15")
Transit timing over three wires with interval ≈ equatorial interval × sec(delta), and observations at lower culmination (α Cyg, β Cas)
Refraction correction from barometer and thermometer (24.04" at z≈23°)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine observing log of meridian-circle work (level/zenith-point determination, star transits, latitude from Pollux). Gauss's observational activity at Göttingen is well documented; nothing mathematically or historically novel here.

checkable.asserts: Saturday level mean, vernier: corrected innen/aussen readings average to 9'10.2"
Sunday level: half of the −1.4" aussen correction applied to each reading
Vernier seconds of Pollux zenith distance after index: 18.7"
Microscope seconds of Pollux z (19.1") plus refraction gives 43.14", close to Gauss's 43.08"
Rough check that mean refraction at z≈23°04' with B=27^z5.1^l, T=11.2°R is about 24" (approximate model)
Sirius: mean of outer wires agrees with middle wire within 0.05 s
Wire-interval ratio Pollux/Sirius ≈ sec δ ratio (difference small)

transcription_corrections: Pollux reduction: '23 14'43"08' should be read 23° 4'43.08" (overwritten digit); sum '51.42.14,15' should be 51°32'14.15".
'b Cassiop' is β Cassiopeiae, observed at lower culmination.
'α Cygni i.P.' denotes the lower culmination of Deneb.
Sunday level line: only the correction '−1"4' is written for 'aussen'; the innen readings are 9'10.0", 3'33.7", 3'16.9".
